details.message: Frontend hooks governing agent sessions and threads (e.g., useSessionStream) do not explicitly inject the `x-workspace-id` header. Consequently, new threads and scripts fall back to the backend's internal state, which may drift from the header selector.

Automation execution endpoints and UI triggers do not strictly bind the header's selected workspace ID (`x-workspace-id`) to the payload or headers. Executions can launch in an unintended workspace if the server context is out of sync.

Tools execute within the context established by the session. Because the initial session creation lacks explicit header-based workspace binding, tools (file reads, bash commands) can resolve to the wrong physical directory.

While changing the header selector immediately updates the frontend `activeWorkspaceId` React state, pending actions from the previous workspace are not explicitly aborted or scoped out, permitting race conditions.
The WorkspaceContext successfully restores the active workspace from the backend (`/api/workspaces`) on reload and falls back safely to the first available workspace if the saved ID is missing.

Event payload streams (NDJSON/SSE) from active Agent Graphs are tied to `sessionId` but do not actively prefix global bus messages with a `workspaceId`. Streams can leak across browser tabs if the UI does not strictly filter them.

recommendations: Inject the `x-workspace-id` HTTP header into all `fetch` calls originating from the Web App's Agent UI (specifically `useSessionStream` and automation hooks).
Refactor `useAutomations` to mandate a `workspaceId` parameter directly from the `WorkspaceContext`.
Add an explicit abort controller to cancel any pending API requests when the Workspace Header Selector value changes.
Enforce `workspaceId` tagging in all server-sent events to allow the frontend to safely ignore events belonging to inactive workspaces.
